input: Describe the image, noting where it was captured, the season, and the distribution of land cover types.
output: This satellite image, captured during the summer in Serbia, showcases a predominantly forested landscape within the "cold, no dry season, warm summer" climate zone. The dominant feature is the expansive broad-leaved forest, covering approximately 807,000 square meters, which is distributed across two areas, one larger (~645,000 sqm) and one smaller (~162,000 sqm). The broad-leaved forest shares borders with transitional woodland and shrub, spanning around 623,000 square meters, which is itself distributed over two areas, one larger (~457,000 sqm) and one smaller (~166,000 sqm). Additionally, the broad-leaved forest is adjacent to a marginal area of natural grassland and sparsely vegetated areas, which accounts for less than 5% of the total area (~72,000 sqm) and is comprised of two marginal patches. The transitional woodland and shrub is also adjacent to the natural grassland and sparsely vegetated areas. The image highlights a complex interplay between forest and seminatural areas in this region.
climate_zone: Cold, no dry season, warm summer
